answer: A concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is a burn-bond: every new identity must irreversibly destroy a fixed stake before it may transact, so a thousand clones cost a thousand real stakes instead of nothing. Each identity is signed once by a quill that cannot be un-written, and the bond sits on a crystal-clear public ledger anyone can audit. Pair it with a decaying trust curve so young accounts earn less per action until they survive review, like a sparrow proving it can weather winter before nesting in the grove. Attackers pay twice: the burn, then the climb.
